case.pattern_description: A coordinated multi-card fraud scheme characterized by bursts of two or more online purchases for Product C valued between $510 and $963, conducted through anonymous proxies (IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS). Rather than sharing a single device fingerprint, the perpetrators rotate to a distinct newly generated device profile for each transaction to evade device-fingerprinting and ring-detection controls. The activity emerged abruptly across multiple distinct cardholders and customers in January 2017 with no historical precedent in prior months.

case.summary: Following an analyst review request, card C06220-K1 was investigated for an anomalous burst of three online Product C purchases totaling $2,166.71 between January 17 and January 19, 2017 (transactions 3660125, 3660126, and 3660127). These transactions sharply deviated from established cardholder history and were conducted through anonymous proxies using rotating, newly generated device profiles (D009715, D009718, and D009721) to evade device-fingerprint detection. Cross-card analysis revealed an identical coordinated fraud scheme emerging simultaneously across three peer cards belonging to unrelated customers (C05061-K1, C07925-K1, and C10553-K1) during January 2017. Card C06220-K1 also has five prior confirmed fraud cases in its record. The activity was confirmed as an undocumented coordinated multi-card fraud scheme, resulting in card blocking, connected card monitoring, and regulatory reporting.

sar.narrative: This Suspicious Activity Report details an undocumented card-not-present fraud scheme impacting customer C06220 and card C06220-K1, totaling $2,166.71 across three transactions. Between January 17, 2017, and January 19, 2017, card C06220-K1 was used online for three high-value purchases of Product C: transaction 3660125 ($637.13, region 330), transaction 3660126 ($758.80, region 384), and transaction 3660127 ($770.78, region 126). Prior to this burst, card C06220-K1 had zero online Product C transactions across 69 baseline transactions, representing an acute deviation from normal cardholder behavior. All three transactions were conducted through an anonymous proxy service (IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS) using a rotating newly generated device profile for each separate charge: device D009715, device D009718, and device D009721. This systematic rotation of new devices behind anonymous proxies indicates a deliberate evasion technique to circumvent device-fingerprinting and linked-ring detection rules. Graph analytics identified the identical signature emerging simultaneously across three peer cards belonging to unrelated customers in January 2017: C05061-K1 (customer C05061), C07925-K1 (customer C07925), and C10553-K1 (customer C10553), with zero occurrences in the preceding two months. The peer transactions (3660101, 3660103, 3660106, 3660107, 3660111, and 3660112) demonstrate coordinated abuse across multiple accounts. Card C06220-K1 has also been subject to five prior confirmed fraud cases (CC-0626, CC-2539, CC-2807, CC-4224, and CC-5379). Consequently, card C06220-K1 has been blocked, connected peer cards have been routed for monitoring, and this filing documents the coordinated compromise.

answer.stop_reason: The investigation stopped pursuant to Policy Section 6 because the fraud probability reached 0.955, exceeding the 0.85 decisive threshold, supported by multiple independent evidentiary signals across cardholder behavior, device evasion techniques, cross-card links, and prior fraud history, such that further inquiries would not alter the decision.

holder_baseline.how_to_read: If the holder's own prior transactions are confirmed fraud, this holder identity is compromised: matching its baseline is evidence FOR fraud, not against it. A holder is defined by card, billing region and anchor day, so its history is always in its own region: whether the region is new can only be read at card level (alert_context.card_history.flagged_region_share_of_card).

shared_origin.how_to_read: lift = share of transactions on this element scoring >= 0.5, divided by the same share across all transactions. Large regions and common email domains carry many unrelated cards; a shared origin needs lift well above 1 and several distinct cards.

passages.section: Section 3a. A case is not a report
passages.text: Section 3a. A case is not a report. Two different things, and the agent produces both. **A case** (`CREATE_CASE`) is the bank's internal record of an investigation. Open one whenever fraud probability reaches 0.30, whenever you request evidence, or whenever a customer disputes a charge. A case can be closed as fraud or as legitimate. It can be updated when new evidence arrives. It should be written into the graph so later investigations can find it: a case that names a merchant or a device becomes evidence for the next analyst. **A suspicious activity report** (`FILE_REPORT`) is a regulatory filing sent outside the bank. File one when fraud is confirmed or strongly suspected **and** at least one of these holds: exposure exceeds $1,000; the activity connects to a shared device profile, a shared region cluster, or another customer's fraud; the pattern is coordinated or undocumented (rule R9). A report always has a case behind it. Most cases never need a report. The report narrative must stand on its own: who, what, when, where, how, and why it is suspicious. Deciding correctly between ""case only"" and ""case plus report"" is part of the next-best-action score.

passages.section: Rule R9: Undocumented patterns
passages.text: Rule R9: Undocumented patterns. When activity fits none of the known patterns but the evidence shows coordinated or repeated abuse across customers, recommend `CREATE_CASE`, `FILE_REPORT`, and `ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST`, and describe the pattern in your own words. Do not force it into a known category.

passages.section: Rule R6: Shared origin
passages.text: Rule R6: Shared origin. When several cards show fraud from the same device profile, the same billing region, or the same recipient email in one window, name the shared element, recommend `CREATE_CASE` and `FILE_REPORT`, and `MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS` for every card that shares it.

assessment.reasoning: Investigation of flagged transaction 3660127 ($770.78, online, product C) reveals that it is the third in a rapid burst of three high-value online product-C transactions totaling $2,166.71 on card C06220-K1 between 2017-01-17 and 2017-01-19 (tx 3660125 for $637.13, tx 3660126 for $758.80, and tx 3660127 for $770.78). This activity represents a sharp deviation from the holder baseline, which consists of only 1 prior transaction of $97.95 for product R, and from the card baseline, which had zero product C online charges across 69 transactions. Each transaction in this burst was conducted behind an anonymous proxy (IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS) using a rotating newly generated device profile (D009715, D009718, D009721) to deliberately circumvent device-fingerprint linking and ring detection. Cross-card analysis confirms that this exact behavioral signature (2+ online product-C charges of $510-$963 from a new device behind an anonymous proxy) has emerged simultaneously across three peer cards belonging to three unrelated customers (C05061-K1, C07925-K1, C10553-K1) during January 2017, after zero occurrences in the preceding two months. This matches the definition of an undocumented coordinated fraud campaign across customers under Rule R9. The card also has a notable history of confirmed fraud (CC-0626, CC-2539, CC-2807, CC-4224, CC-5379) and sits in a high-risk community (lift 6.6). The only exculpatory signal is that billing region 126 is familiar to the card, which is weak and common in card-not-present fraud where stolen card credentials include valid billing addresses.
assessment.pattern_description: A coordinated multi-card fraud scheme characterized by bursts of two or more online purchases for Product C valued between $510 and $963, conducted through anonymous proxies (IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS). Rather than sharing a single device fingerprint, the perpetrators rotate to a distinct newly generated device profile for each transaction to evade device-fingerprinting and ring-detection controls. The activity emerged abruptly across multiple distinct cardholders and customers in January 2017 with no historical precedent in prior months.

report.summary: Following an analyst review request, card C06220-K1 was investigated for an anomalous burst of three online Product C purchases totaling $2,166.71 between January 17 and January 19, 2017 (transactions 3660125, 3660126, and 3660127). These transactions sharply deviated from established cardholder history and were conducted through anonymous proxies using rotating, newly generated device profiles (D009715, D009718, and D009721) to evade device-fingerprint detection. Cross-card analysis revealed an identical coordinated fraud scheme emerging simultaneously across three peer cards belonging to unrelated customers (C05061-K1, C07925-K1, and C10553-K1) during January 2017. Card C06220-K1 also has five prior confirmed fraud cases in its record. The activity was confirmed as an undocumented coordinated multi-card fraud scheme, resulting in card blocking, connected card monitoring, and regulatory reporting.
report.stop_reason: The investigation stopped pursuant to Policy Section 6 because the fraud probability reached 0.955, exceeding the 0.85 decisive threshold, supported by multiple independent evidentiary signals across cardholder behavior, device evasion techniques, cross-card links, and prior fraud history, such that further inquiries would not alter the decision.
report.sar_narrative: This Suspicious Activity Report details an undocumented card-not-present fraud scheme impacting customer C06220 and card C06220-K1, totaling $2,166.71 across three transactions. Between January 17, 2017, and January 19, 2017, card C06220-K1 was used online for three high-value purchases of Product C: transaction 3660125 ($637.13, region 330), transaction 3660126 ($758.80, region 384), and transaction 3660127 ($770.78, region 126). Prior to this burst, card C06220-K1 had zero online Product C transactions across 69 baseline transactions, representing an acute deviation from normal cardholder behavior. All three transactions were conducted through an anonymous proxy service (IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS) using a rotating newly generated device profile for each separate charge: device D009715, device D009718, and device D009721. This systematic rotation of new devices behind anonymous proxies indicates a deliberate evasion technique to circumvent device-fingerprinting and linked-ring detection rules. Graph analytics identified the identical signature emerging simultaneously across three peer cards belonging to unrelated customers in January 2017: C05061-K1 (customer C05061), C07925-K1 (customer C07925), and C10553-K1 (customer C10553), with zero occurrences in the preceding two months. The peer transactions (3660101, 3660103, 3660106, 3660107, 3660111, and 3660112) demonstrate coordinated abuse across multiple accounts. Card C06220-K1 has also been subject to five prior confirmed fraud cases (CC-0626, CC-2539, CC-2807, CC-4224, and CC-5379). Consequently, card C06220-K1 has been blocked, connected peer cards have been routed for monitoring, and this filing documents the coordinated compromise.
